Pick your hull, and tap an ally's avatar to pick theirs.

cards.name: Scarab Rally
cards.description: Scarabs only, no ball - just you, your throttle and a course of rings. Hold the throttle to wind up speed, drift the hairpins to keep it, and juke into a mouth that sits off your line. Walls to weave and danger beside the fast line on the hard levels. First team to put a pilot through the last ring takes it.

cards.name: Scarab Scramble
cards.description: Every bright crystal you fly through becomes YOUR ball. Roll it, bat it, bank it off the walls and through any glowing ring - first team to ten. Bumping enemy balls is always safe defense, and a juke dash steals one outright. Scarab only. Easy to start, hard to stop.

cards.name: Tollway
cards.description: Plants grow in the court, and a ring can only be grafted onto one. Fly at a plant, plant your ring at its foot, then drive a ball across the court and through the mouth - and every ball that threads it, yours or theirs or a stray off the wall, pays YOU and raises a monument on the spot, so the arena gets built out of the scoring. Rings are spent when they pay, so keep planting. Scarab only. First team to 3 tolls.

cards.name: Undertow
cards.description: Scarabs only, loose in the wildlife cages, with no guns anywhere. Dash beside a rival and the cavitation plate drags them through the undertow - every element they have stripped for four seconds. Drag the swarm through it too and the creatures die. A pilot is three points, a creature one; first team to the target wins.

cards.name: Wrecking Ball
cards.description: Scarabs only, in a walled court grown full of cacti and coral. Fly through a bright crystal and it becomes your ball - bowl it into the thickest stand and every prism it plows through is yours; flick a dash beside the forest and the cavitation plate shreds the rest. Balls bounce off the wall and come back for more. First team to the wrecking target wins.

vessels.name: Thresher
vessels.description: A small, nimble hull towing a heavy wrecking ball on a chain. Turn hard and snap back and the ball whips round; wind the chain out and let it reel in, and it cracks red-hot through everything. Plant it and swing round it to sling yourself off.

Charge.description: The ball itself - PASSIVE, always destructive, and its destruction is binary. Below smash speed it wears your DOMAIN colour, destroys rival prisms it touches and BOUNCES off your own domain's; at smash speed it turns RED, destroys every prism it hits (yours included) and every hit sets off an explosion. The ball and the chain also reach ENEMY VESSELS: each contact is a scored Strike that STEALS petals (the PvP-is-petals-only rule). Charge scales how many: ThresherConfigSO.vesselHitPetals, 1 petal per element at rest -> 3 at level 10 (floor 0.5).

upgrade.label: Magnet
upgrade.description: The free ball is drawn toward the nearest enemy vessel within magnetRange (150 u) at magnetAcceleration (220 u/s^2) - it moves only your ball, never the other vessel. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Charge) in ThresherExecutor (MagnetActive -> PullBallToEnemy).

words.does: Your chained ball smashes rival prisms and bounces off your own. Swung to smash speed it turns red and blows up every prism it hits, yours too. Ball or chain striking a rival steals their petals.
words.scales: More Charge steals more petals with every strike on a rival.

Mass.description: The A button TOGGLES Mass Mode: the ball builds instead of breaking. It STEALS the rival prisms it touches, SHIELDS your own, lays a trail of your prisms behind it and never explodes - and the energy the chain's kills bank keeps building instead of being spent, so leaving Mass Mode makes the next rival hit a bigger blast. Mass scales the SIZE of the trail prisms the ball lays: ThresherConfigSO.massTrailScale on every axis of massTrailPrismScale, x1 at rest -> x2 at level 10 (floor x0.5).

upgrade.label: Armoured Trail
upgrade.description: The prisms the ball lays in Mass Mode are laid SHIELDED (per-lay snapshot). Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Mass) in ThresherExecutor.LayTrailPrism (ArmouredTrailActive).

words.does: Switch the ball from breaking to building: it steals rival prisms it touches, shields your own and lays your trail behind it, never exploding. The energy it banks makes a bigger blast once you switch back.
words.scales: More Mass makes the trail prisms the ball lays bigger.

Space.description: The RIGHT trigger is the chain's RIGIDITY (analog): released, the chain is a slack bungee the turns and the spin carry the ball out on; pulled, it is rigid. Tightening reels the ball in and spins it up - the crack - and the chain eases to lime when a tighten now would crack it past smash speed. The chain, taut or slack, SLICES rival prisms it touches and SHIELDS your own; each kill banks energy for the ball's next explosion (the Space card shows how much radius is banked). Space scales the LARGEST explosion the bank can buy: ThresherConfigSO.energyMaxDiameterScale, x4 diameter at rest -> x8 at level 10 (floor x2).

upgrade.label: Breaker
upgrade.description: A RED (smash-speed) ball's direct hit destroys super-shielded prisms, through the sanctioned DeactivateShields -> Damage(devastate) sequence. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Space) in ThresherExecutor.SweepBall (BreakerActive). (Until 2026-10-13 Space 5 was Reaper Chain.)

words.does: Stiffen the chain: let go and it is a slack bungee, pull and it goes rigid, reeling the ball in and cracking it up to speed. The chain slices rival prisms and shields yours, banking energy for the ball's next explosion.
words.scales: More Space raises the biggest explosion your banked energy can buy.

Time.description: The LEFT trigger is a BRAKE (analog): a partial pull slows the ball and swings you round it like a sliding anchor; only a FULL pull stops it, smoothly, and makes it the pivot you orbit, faster every lap (pull RT to wind in and spin faster). With both triggers at a full pull the camera hands over to the launch view: the sticks pick a launch point on the circle and easing LT off launches from it, through the crosshair, as the ship comes round - always boosted (launchBoost x4.8), whatever the timing. Your hull lays no trail while the crosshair is up. Time scales how fast the spin winds up to launch speed: ThresherConfigSO.spinMultiplier on the spin-up rate AND its cap, x1 at rest -> x1.75 at level 10 (floor x0.5).

upgrade.description: OPEN since 2026-10-13 (design needed). Time 5 was "Perfect Release" (a launch timed inside a 0.25 s window left x1.6 faster); it retired when EVERY aimed launch out of the crosshair view took the boost (ThresherConfigSO.launchBoost, x4.8) - the crosshair move is rewarded, not the timing. No IsUpgradeActive(Time) gate remains.

words.does: Brake the ball: a partial pull swings you round it like a sliding anchor, a full pull plants it as a pivot you orbit faster every lap. Pull both triggers fully to aim, then ease off to launch boosted.
words.scales: More Time winds the spin up to launch speed faster.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Tilt the phone to steer with no thumb down.
Touch overrides on the prefab: Idle = Touch Launch, OnlyRightStick = Winch, OnlyLeftStick = Plant.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

omni.label: windmills the ball round the ship

words.ability: windmills the ball round the ship
words.does: For 12 seconds your red-hot wrecking ball circles the ship across your line of flight, smashing what it sweeps; the winch still sets its size.

cards.name: Harvest
cards.description: Threshers only - a field of sheaves floating in every direction, each a core of blocks bristling with stalks. Press A to leave Mass Mode and break. Mow the stalks with your chain to charge the ball, then whip it into the core and the charge goes off as one blast. Only prisms that are not your colour count. Crystals in the clear centre windmill your red-hot ball round you. Higher intensities shield the cores, colour the sheaves by team and add danger stalks. First team to the harvest target wins.

cards.name: Jackstraw
cards.description: Threshers only - a brawl in a heap of pick-up sticks floating in every direction. Each stick is about a chain long, so your swinging ball is always about to clip one, and every stick it breaks costs it speed. Run your ball or chain through a rival pilot to strike them - each strike is one point and silences them while they refuel. Crystals float in the clearings, out of the sticks' cover. Higher intensities grow the heap, cross the sticks into jacks and add red-tipped sticks. First team to the target wins.

cards.name: Thresher Time
cards.description: Threshers only, against the clock. Every gate is a nest to break - the ball, a chain cut, a charged blast or a ram all crack its core, and the gate opens. Plant beside a nest and your orbiting chain shreds its cage and charges the ball, then let go and smash the core. Every third nest hides a crystal. Higher levels arm the cage with danger and shielded plates and regrow it fast. Fastest domain home wins.

vessels.name: Stoat
vessels.description: Never flies straight for long. In Mass mode the triggers lay a wormhole dipole ahead - a sink and a source you fly through - and a thick trail behind; in Time mode they lay an attractor to orbit and sling off a quarter-turn round. Every pair that dies throws a space-time ripple that strips rivals.

Charge.description: Passive, anti-vessel and anti-creature. Every pair of yours that annihilates - a dipole let go, an orbit's pair closing after its slingshot - throws a SPACE-TIME RIPPLE from where the poles met: a spherical wave that bends the scene as it passes. Where its front sweeps over them, rival vessels are STRIPPED of one whole petal of every element they hold (shed as crystals around them; a ward against blasts stops it) and creatures are killed. It touches no prism, and never you or a teammate. The ripple's reach is the separation the poles had when you let go (x0.6, 30 -> 160 u) - Charge scales it x1 -> x2 at level 10 (StoatRippleConfigSO.reach, replicated level).

upgrade.label: Siphon
upgrade.description: The petals the ripple strips come straight to YOU instead of being shed as crystals - a rival's level becomes yours. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Charge), replicated, so every peer moves the same petals (StoatRippleConfigSO.siphonOnChargeUpgrade).

words.does: Whenever one of your hole pairs collapses, it throws a space-time ripple that strips a petal of every element from each rival it sweeps over and kills creatures. It never touches prisms, you or teammates.
words.scales: More Charge makes the ripple reach further.

Mass.description: Passive. Your launch out of an orbit hits harder: Mass is its momentum - one dial, read live: the launch kick x1 at rest -> x2.5 at level 10 (StoatSlingConfigSO.launchPower). Aim it by flicking or steering as you let go.

upgrade.label: Armoured Wake
upgrade.description: The prisms you lay while a launch's kick lasts (1.5 s) arrive SHIELDED. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Mass), replicated: every peer runs the replicated release, so every peer lays the same tier (StoatSlingConfigSO.massUpgradeShieldsLaunchTrail).

words.does: Your launch out of an orbit hits harder. Let go or flick your steering thumb to fly out of the orbit, aimed where you flick or steer, and the kick carries more momentum.
words.scales: More Mass makes the launch kick harder.

Space.description: Triggers: LT the left orbit, RT the right. A press lays a light black hole and its white hole ahead of you, the black hole on the pressed side, spinning clockwise on the right and anti-clockwise on the left. Fly past it on that side and it catches you, then draws you in to its inner orbit and carries you round a little faster. Squeeze harder for a tighter circle. Let go, or FLICK your steering thumb, to launch: toward where you flick or steer, up to 60 degrees off the orbit, the whole kick a quarter-turn round. The pair then falls together and annihilates, throwing the Charge ripple. A pair you own never pulls you in. Space is the pair's reach - one dial, read live: the orbit's radius x1 -> x1.4 at level 10 (StoatSlingConfigSO.orbitReach). R_VesselActions/STOAT_DIPOLE.md section 1b.

upgrade.label: Accretion
upgrade.description: While you orbit, rival prisms that fall into your attractor are STOLEN (yours), and each one adds 4% to the reach of the ripple that pair throws, up to +40% (StoatSlingConfigSO.accretionPerPrism / accretionMax).

words.does: Lay a black hole and its white hole ahead, the black hole on the side you pressed. Fly past it on that side and it catches you into an orbit: squeeze for a tighter circle, let go or flick to launch where you aim.
words.trigger: Press, hold to orbit, release or flick to launch
words.scales: More Space widens the orbit your hole pair catches you into.

Time.description: Passive speed. While a pair is held your flight clock warps and you fly faster: x2.7 at rest, 15% more while the orbit holds you. Let go a quarter-turn after the catch (90 deg +- 15) for the whole launch kick, a fifth of it outside that window; the orbit's dotted circle turns lime inside it. Time is rate - one dial, the Stoat's warp: x2.7 at rest -> x5.6 at level 10 (StoatDipoleConfigSO.boost x StoatSlingConfigSO.catchWarpShare).

upgrade.label: Foresight
upgrade.description: You also see the predicted paths of the three nearest rivals within 1500 u, in their domain colours - each flown 500 u forward on the turn and speed it is holding right now, measured from its pose (no input needed). Read a rival's line and lay your pair across it. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Time), replicated; drawn for the local pilot only (StoatPathfinderExecutor.Foresight).

words.does: While you orbit, your clock warps and you fly faster. Let go about a quarter-turn after the catch, when the dotted circle turns lime, for the full slingshot kick; any other moment gives only a fraction.
words.scales: More Time speeds up the orbit's warp and strengthens the slingshot kick.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

rows.touch: Shown on its card, no press

notes: Phone: buttons round the right thumb; lifting a thumb fires nothing.
Touch overrides on the prefab: RightStick = Sling Right, LeftStick = Sling Left, Button1 = Hold.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Fires a branching thunderbolt from your cell's centre that sets prisms along it burning; any omni crystal a branch reaches sends off a smaller bolt of its own.

cards.name: Regatta
cards.description: Every hull, one circuit, three laps. Three rails run the racing line in the three team colours - an Urchin grinds the one in its colour and a Squirrel skims it, while a Manta, a Rhino, a Scarab or a Sparrow flies beside it. Thread the rings in order - every gate anyone on your team threads counts. The race ends when the first pilot finishes; the team with the most gates wins. Pick your hull, and tap an ally's avatar to pick theirs.

cards.name: Slingshot
cards.description: Stoats only. You cruise slow and turn wide - your poles do the steering. Squeeze LT and RT to hold a black hole and a white hole open ahead of you - the difference pulls them apart sideways, the sum lengthways - and the field bends your path round the corner. Dive into the black hole and you come out of the white one. Eight rings, two laps.

vessels.name: Brittle Star
vessels.description: A one-touch flyer built round a cockpit and a five-pointed support ring. Swap between Speed, Creation, Space and Charge modes - five guns that overheat, or five cords that whip and stiffen into sabers - turn the ring to bring a turret to bear, and throw spare rings as bombs.

Charge.description: Y. FIVE CORDS, one from each turret, slicing every prism they touch (any domain; your own fresh trail is spared) and striking rival hulls for petals. Released, RT leaves them WHIPS at 150% length: heavy, inextensible, slow - a turn, a ring flick or a sweep of the right stick sends a wave travelling down them that rings on for seconds. Pulled, RT shortens them to 100% and stiffens them into five SABERS that keep 60% of the whip's give (analog: every depth in between). The right stick turns them with the ring and opens them out. Using them cools the guns. LT throws the ring - only with a SPARE ring in stock (one per crystal, two at most); the mounted ring then regrows on its own. It blows on contact or its fuse in a disk as wide as the cell's nucleus, bursting out of the ring as faceted volumes - five coiling arms led by crystals, five crests and the ring's own pentagon - still spinning, destroying every prism within 40 u of the blast and every prism in its plane and stripping petals from every rival hull it crosses (petals only - nothing is moved). The card shows the spare stock. Charge is threat - one dial: the cords' cut width and the rounds' size x1 -> x1.8 at level 10 (projectileScaleMultiplier), the disk's thickness x1 -> x4 on top of its x4 base, 4 to 16 times the ring's (blastScale).

upgrade.label: Thrown Sabers
upgrade.description: With the cords held RIGID (RT held, the cords fully out), LT cuts all five off and throws them along the lines they point - the right stick aims them as it aims the cords: centred they converge ahead, pushed they fan out. Each flies on tumbling end over end, cutting every prism it crosses and striking rival hulls for petals, then is gone; new cords grow back after a moment. The ring is thrown only when the sabers cannot be (BrittleStarConfigSO.thrownSaber*).

words.does: Five cords, one per turret, slice prisms and strike rival hulls for petals: loose whips, or stiff sabers while you fire. With a spare ring, throw the ring to burst a spinning disk that wrecks every prism in its plane.
words.scales: More Charge widens the cords' cut, grows the rounds and thickens the thrown ring's blast disk.

Mass.description: B. A trail behind EACH of the ring's five corners instead of the single small block from the cockpit - the same small block, five lines that turn with the ring's firing rotation. The SLOWEST mode: cruise x0.5. Mass is girth - one dial: the width and height of EVERY block you lay, the base trail's and the corner trails', x1 -> x2 at level 10, never their length (BrittleStarConfigSO.prismWidthScale).

upgrade.label: Shielded Trail
upgrade.description: Every ordinary prism the hull lays arrives SHIELDED - the base trail's and Creation Mode's five corner trails' alike (danger prisms stay danger prisms).

words.does: Lay a trail behind each of the ring's five corners instead of one behind the cockpit, the five lines turning with the ring. The slowest mode: you cruise at half speed.
words.scales: More Mass makes every block you lay wider and taller, never longer.

Space.description: X. FIVE GUNS: RT fires every turret, its pull setting the rate (analog, up to 90 rounds/s each; the Sparrow's round at 135 u/s, swelling as it flies, 387 u reach). The right stick's direction turns the ring, and the guns with it; its deflection moves them in and out: centred they meet 120 u ahead (the vessel a crosshair), pushed to the rim they splay 25 degrees. In every other mode RT fires the one turret the ring has turned to the aim, the same gun with no spread. Every round HEATS the guns - heat per second is the pull x the guns firing - and overheated they cannot fire until they cool; overheated in Space Mode your trail lays DANGER prisms. The card shows the heat. Friendly fire is on. A round on a rival hull is a scored bullet hit (petals only). Space is reach and endurance: every gun's range x1 -> x2 at level 10 (BrittleStarConfigSO.rangeMultiplier), and the heat the guns hold x1 -> x3.33, so a full five-gun burst runs ~6 s at level 0 and ~20 s at level 10 (BrittleStarConfigSO.heatCapacity).

upgrade.label: Explosive Rounds
upgrade.description: Every round a prism stops BURSTS, destroying the prisms within 10 u of where it struck (any domain - friendly fire; your own fresh trail is spared; a shield pops first). The round's own hit on a hull is the scored hit, as before (BrittleStarConfigSO.explosiveRoundRadius).

words.does: All five guns fire together, converged ahead or splayed by your aim, and rounds that hit rival hulls take petals. Firing heats the guns; overheated they stop, and your trail lays danger prisms.
words.trigger: Tap to switch mode, hold to fire
words.scales: More Space gives every gun longer range and lets the guns hold more heat before they overheat.

Time.description: A. Ignite every thruster: the hull's cruise speed x6, the base trail's spacing stretched by the same ratio so production per second does not rise, and every prism stretched with it so the trail still joins up. Time is rate - one dial: Speed Mode's multiplier x6 -> x8 at level 10 (BrittleStarConfigSO.speedModeMultiplier).

upgrade.label: Speed Roll
upgrade.description: In Speed Mode the right stick ROLLS the hull instead of turning the ring: its x rolls about the nose (220 deg/s), its y pulls the nose (90 deg/s), so the hull can roll and pull to change direction at Speed Mode's speed (BrittleStarConfigSO.speedRoll*).

words.does: Ignite every thruster for a big jump in cruise speed. The trail spreads out and stretches so it still joins up, without laying more prisms per second.
words.scales: More Time makes Speed Mode faster still.

notes: Phone: buttons round the right thumb; lifting a thumb fires nothing.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Adds a spare ring to your stock, up to two, so you can throw your ring for a ring explosion.

cards.name: Brittle Star Time
cards.description: Brittle Stars only, against the clock. Speed Mode runs you at six times cruise - but it turns wide. Every intensity asks one question of it. Gearbox - hold Speed or shift down. Feather slalom - tap it in and out to weave. Coast-in hairpins - let go early and coast into the turn. Corkscrew - start at Time 5 and roll to hold Speed through the coil. Two laps. Fastest domain home wins.

cards.name: Flatline
cards.description: Brittle Stars only - a duel through thin panes of prisms. A pane stops your rounds, but your cords cut straight through it, so nobody is safe behind one. Fly round the loose panes, through the tunnels and into the cages. Throw your ring face-on into a pane and it bursts flat along it - get off a pane when a ring comes spinning at you. A round on a rival is one point and a cord strike is eight; the ring scores nothing. Crystals inside the rooms give you spare rings. First team to 90 wins.

cards.name: Shatterplane
cards.description: Brittle Stars only - break the plates hanging in the cell. Your guns chip any plate from any angle, but square up to a plate and throw your ring, and its flat blast erases the whole plate. A few degrees off, it only cuts a stripe. Every crystal is a spare ring and floats on the axis of a plate, so taking one lines you up. First team to break the target wins.

vessels.name: Angler
vessels.description: The fleet's strategist. Hold the lure light out to draw wild fauna, tame the ones you hold, and lead them as a school of two halves. Paint the prisms you want gone with RT, erase mistakes with LT, and let go to throw one half at what you painted; the next paint sends the other half.

Charge.description: LT, held: a narrow beam from the nose unpaints prisms (an already-ordered one leaves every order). Each time the beam comes onto a rival vessel - another one, or the same one again - it LOCKS, and the lock SPENDS one creature: it leaves your school (your count drops by one) and chases that vessel until it dies, each bite a scored contact Strike that takes petals. Charge sets how often a hunter bites: once a second at Charge 0, every 0.4 s at Charge 10 (AnglerConfigSO.biteRate). R_VesselActions/ANGLER.md.

upgrade.label: Swallow
upgrade.description: A hunter's bite no longer knocks the petals loose: they land on you. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Charge).

words.does: A narrow beam unpaints prisms. Sweep it onto a rival vessel to lock on: one creature leaves your school and chases that vessel until it dies, every bite taking petals.
words.scales: Charge does not change this ability yet.

Mass.description: A (Space on a keyboard), held: the esca lights and the hull stops. Wild herbivores in its reach turn to it, and one held in the light for the taming time joins your school (the count on this card). Plants in the light grow three times as fast. Let go, and any seed an omni crystal left is planted at the esca, in your domain. Mass sets the light's size: its reach and hold grow x1 at Mass 0 to x2 at Mass 10 (AnglerConfigSO.lureScale).

upgrade.label: Steal Fauna
upgrade.description: The lure takes creatures from other holders too: another Angler's tamed fauna can be lured, tamed and kept. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Mass).

words.does: Light the lure and stop: wild herbivores in reach turn to you, and one held in the light long enough joins your school. Plants in the light grow faster; let go to plant any seed an omni crystal left.
words.scales: Mass does not change this ability yet.

Space.description: RT, held: a beam reaching 3200 u (and close up, at the nose) paints prisms, which light up, and every creature prefers them; half your school balls up ahead, any of that half still in flight included. Let go: each creature of that half flies at the most recently painted prisms first, at any distance, and eats them, and the next paint sends the other half. Lit prisms stay lit until eaten or erased. Space sets the brush's width: x1 at Space 0 to x2 at Space 10 (AnglerConfigSO.brushScale).

upgrade.label: Paint Shields
upgrade.description: The brush paints shielded prisms too, and the squad cracks a painted prism's shield off when it arrives, so it can be eaten. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Space).

words.does: A long beam paints prisms, which light up while half your school balls up ahead. Let go to throw that half at the newest painted prisms to eat them; the next throw sends the other half.
words.scales: Space does not change this ability yet.

Time.description: B (T on a keyboard): the hull dashes 75% of the way to the centre of one half of your school, measured when pressed, in 0.35 s; the next dash goes to the other half, so you fly between your two groups. Time also speeds your tamed fauna: x1 at Time 0 to x2 at Time 10 (AnglerConfigSO.faunaSpeed).

upgrade.label: Riptide
upgrade.description: A dash pressed while one is in flight is kept and fires the moment it lands, at your other group, so you chain between your two groups. Gated on IsUpgradeActive(Time).

words.does: Dash most of the way to the centre of one half of your school in a blink; the next dash goes to the other half, so you hop between your two groups.
words.scales: More Time makes your tamed creatures swim faster.

notes: Phone: buttons round the right thumb; lifting a thumb fires nothing.
Touch overrides on the prefab: RightStick = Paint, LeftStick = Erase.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: The crystal turns into a random creature that joins your school, and leaves a plant seed that is planted in your colour the next time you let go of the lure.

cards.name: Glasshouse
cards.description: Anglers only - a timed garden. Every omni crystal is a creature and a seed. Let go of the lure and the seed is planted in your colour, and the lure light grows every plant in reach three times as fast. Your score is the mass standing in your colour when the clock runs out - your trail and your garden. Wild herds graze every garden outside the core, and a rival paints your plants to throw a school at them. Higher intensities thin the seeds, bring more grazers and leave less room to grow.

cards.name: Kelpwood
cards.description: Anglers only - a hunt through a ball of kelp, strands reaching out from the core in every direction. Sweep your eraser onto a rival pilot to lock them - one creature leaves your school and hunts them, and every bite is a point that silences them. Tame the herds grazing the kelp, or take an omni crystal, to grow your school; dash to your other group to shake a hunter. Higher intensities thicken the kelp, thin the herds and crystals, and add danger tips and collars. First team to the target wins.

cards.name: Lantern Run
cards.description: Anglers only, and you paint your own path. Every leg holds two clusters of prism mass, one for each half of your school. Hold RT on the near one and let go to throw, paint the far one past the ring and throw again, then dash after each half and zoom straight through the ring. The clusters grow back. Two laps. Fastest domain home wins.

vessels.name: Goby
vessels.description: Two seats, one hull, like a goby and the pistol shrimp it shares a burrow with. One player flies the Goby, the hull, on two thumbs and lays the path; the other rides that path side on as the Pistol, a sidescroller - diving down the hills, launching into clusters and firing vortex rings. D-pad left or right swaps seats; the AI takes the empty one.
vessels.note: the Goby & Pistol crew vessel (two subvessels, one hull class): .claude/skills/duo-vessel; moved off 16 (BrittleStar)

Charge.description: A vortex ring from the Pistol's Snap that hits a rival hull takes petals from each of its elements; Charge raises how many (GobyPistolConfig ringPetals, 1 at rest -> 3 at level 10). While the Goby holds a lock on a rival that is on the Pistol's screen, the ring flies at it.
notes: UPGRADE IS PROSE — no live IsUpgradeActive gate

words.does: The Pistol's Snap fires a vortex ring that sweeps up rival prisms and smashes them as it collapses; a ring that hits a rival hull takes petals. If the Goby holds a lock on a rival in the Pistol's view, the ring homes in.
words.scales: More Charge makes each ring hit take more petals from every one of a rival's elements.

Mass.description: At each perch the Pistol rests and builds a den of prisms and shielded prisms, as many as the distance it travelled since its last den and Mass make (denMassScale, x1 at rest -> x2.5 at level 10). It can ride back to an old den to add to it.

upgrade.label: Fortress
upgrade.description: Dens also grow danger prisms and super-shielded prisms.

words.does: At each perch the Pistol rests and builds a den of prisms and shielded prisms, bigger the more energy it earned flying over its ground. It can ride back to add to an old den; a fall loses the energy.
words.trigger: Passive - the Pistol rests at a perch
words.scales: More Mass builds more den prisms from the same energy.

Space.description: Mass either side of the Pistol's plane is pulled into it, from further with Space (pullReach, 40 u at rest -> 200 u at level 10). Danger, super-shielded and the pair's own prisms never move.

upgrade.label: Deep Undertow
upgrade.description: Shielded prisms are pulled in too.

words.does: Mass either side of the Pistol's plane is pulled into it, and crystals drift in for the Pistol to collect. Danger, super-shielded and your own prisms never move.
words.scales: More Space pulls mass in from further away and widens the hull's skim reach.

Time.description: Time shortens the cooldown of the Pistol's jump, the burst of speed that flings it off its ground (jumpCooldown, 9 s at rest -> 3 s at level 10).

upgrade.label: Phase Dart
upgrade.description: The Goby's darts pass through prisms.

words.does: Switched off: the Pistol's aimed jump is disabled in the Goby and Pistol config, so nothing fires it right now, neither a player nor the AI. Its level-5 upgrade is wired for when it returns.
words.scales: Time has nothing to act on while the jump is off.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

list.name: Goby
list.role: The 3D flier. Two thumbs; lays the path the Pistol rides and perches at its ends.

abilities.name: Lock
abilities.text: Locks the best target in the nose's cone, rival vessels first, then fauna; while the lock is on the Pistol's screen its rings home on it.

abilities.name: Perches
abilities.text: Passive: a dart's end becomes a perch once it is 900 u from the last one; the Pistol builds its den there.

abilities.name: Dart
abilities.text: Hold to charge the distance (140 to 600 u over 0.8 s), let go to dart; it stops on the first block on its line.

list.name: Pistol
list.role: The 2D sidescroller. Rides the islands side on, bound to the Goby's path, and breaks through every block but the Goby's trail.

abilities.name: Ghost
abilities.text: A moment of passing through prisms, then a cooldown.

cards.name: Perch Run
cards.description: Goby only, and every ring is a dart. Hold to charge, let go, and the Goby flies that far in one second, so the fewer darts the faster. Watch the reach ring - it shows where you will stop. Hairpins punish a full charge, coral stops a dart aimed at the centre (take the rim), and on the hardest level two rings on one line fall to a single dart. First team to put a pilot through the last ring takes it.

vessels.name: Wrasse
vessels.description: Two seats, one hull, like a cleaner wrasse and the grouper it keeps clean. One player flies the Grouper, the hull; the other flies the Wrasse, a kite on the hull's own plane - its head picks enemy prisms off, its tail lassos motes into blasts, prism clusters, saved boosts and crystal rams. D-pad left or right swaps seats; the AI takes the empty one.
vessels.note: a cleaner wrasse and its host: the Sparrow hull with the Kite & Tail navigator seat (two players, one hull): Controller/Vessel/Crew/KITE_NAVIGATOR.md

Charge.description: Loops of Charge motes power the kite's ram: strike a rival hull to knock its crystals loose, or strike wildlife. The card counts the rams held.

upgrade.label: Crystal Steal
upgrade.description: A ram steals the rival's crystals instead of knocking them loose.

notes: UPGRADE IS PROSE — no live IsUpgradeActive gate
NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: The Wrasse's kite loops its tail round Charge motes to power its ram: a charged ram on a rival hull knocks petals loose as crystals anyone can grab, and kills a creature it passes through.
words.trigger: Passive - loop Charge motes, then ram
words.scales: More Charge makes Charge motes turn up more often on the kite's board.

Mass.description: A loop of Mass motes lays a cluster of prisms on the kite's plane. The card flashes when one is laid.

upgrade.label: Shielded Clusters
upgrade.description: Mass clusters are laid shielded.

notes: UPGRADE IS PROSE — no live IsUpgradeActive gate (every gate is authored off on this hull)
NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: The Wrasse's kite closes its tail round Mass motes to lay a cluster of your prisms on its plane; the more motes in one loop, the far bigger the cluster. A loop holding two elements fizzles.
words.scales: More Mass makes Mass motes turn up more often on the kite's board.

Space.description: The kite closes a loop of Space motes and a blast goes off where it closed; a bigger loop, a bigger blast. The card counts what the last blast destroyed.

upgrade.label: Shield Breaker
upgrade.description: Space blasts destroy shielded and super-shielded prisms.

notes: UPGRADE IS PROSE — no live IsUpgradeActive gate

words.does: The Wrasse's kite closes its tail round Space motes and a blast goes off where the loop closed, destroying rival prisms and sparing yours; the more motes in the loop, the bigger the blast.
words.scales: More Space makes Space motes turn up more often and widens the hull's skim reach.

Time.description: Every loop of Time motes the kite closes saves boosts for the pilot. The pilot spends them on the trigger; the card counts how many are saved.
notes: UPGRADE IS PROSE — no live IsUpgradeActive gate

words.does: Each loop of Time motes the Wrasse's kite closes saves boosts for the Grouper. The Grouper's pilot spends them one at a time, each a short burst of speed, and can chain them back to back.
words.scales: More Time makes Time motes turn up more often and makes each boost faster.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Drops a cluster of motes of every element on the navigator's board for the kite to lasso, making up for a short supply of crystals.

list.name: Grouper
list.role: The pilot. Flies the hull on two sticks: the Sparrow's hull with its guns, missiles and buttons removed.

abilities.name: Saved Boosts
abilities.text: RT spends a boost the Wrasse saved.

list.name: Wrasse
list.role: The navigator. A kite on the hull's own plane, held on an invisible rope by every input; its tail lassos motes of one element and a closed loop fires that element.

abilities.name: Time loops
abilities.text: A loop of Time motes saves boosts for the Grouper to spend.

cards.name: Wrasse Run
cards.description: The Wrasse collects the rings. Grouper, fly your plane through the lit ring so the Wrasse can swing through it - the hull alone does not count. Wrasse, loop Time motes to bank boosts the Grouper spends to reach the next ring. Two laps. Fastest crew home wins.

vessels.name: Orca
vessels.description: Four seats, one hull - a helm and three gunners. The helm flies with two thumbs, boosts on the right trigger and rings the hull in danger prisms on the left; each gunner looks out of a stabilized turret and flies the missile it releases. Every empty seat is flown by the AI. Keys 1-4 or the D-pad change seat.
vessels.note: the 4-seat vessel: one helm and three gunner seats on one hull, every empty seat an AI: Controller/Vessel/Crew/ORCA_CREW.md

Charge.description: Each gunner launches missiles from its own magazine and flies them by hand; Charge makes them faster and sharper. An omni crystal gives every gunner a missile. The card counts your missiles.

words.does: Each gunner launches missiles from its own magazine and steers them by hand; a missile collects crystals it flies through. An omni crystal gives every gunner one more missile.
words.trigger: Gunner seats - tap to launch, then steer
words.scales: More Charge makes the missiles fly faster and turn sharper.

Mass.description: The helm rings the hull in super-shielded prisms, open ahead, on the left trigger; they ride with the hull, then drop where they are as danger prisms. Mass carries the ring longer. The card shows its recharge.

words.does: The helm rings the hull in super-shielded prisms, open ahead, that ride with it for a few seconds, then drop where they stand as danger prisms that linger.
words.scales: More Mass carries the shield ring with the hull for longer before it drops.

Space.description: A missile bursts on contact, after five seconds, or when its gunner presses Missile again, and the third gunner's bomb bursts the same way; Space widens both blasts. The card flashes on every burst.

words.does: A missile bursts on contact, after five seconds, or when its gunner taps again, wrecking rival prisms nearby and taking petals from rival hulls; the bomb gunner's bomb bursts the same way.
words.trigger: On contact, on its fuse, or tap again
words.scales: More Space widens the missile and bomb blasts and the hull's skim reach.

Time.description: The helm boosts on the right trigger while the tank lasts; it refills on its own, faster with Time. The card shows the tank.

words.does: The helm boosts while the tank lasts, and the tank refills on its own.
words.scales: More Time refills the tank faster and makes the boost faster.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Every gunner seat gets one more missile in its magazine, whether the hull or a gunner's missile took the crystal.

list.name: Helm
list.role: Flies the hull with two thumbs. RT boosts while the tank lasts; LT raises the shield.

list.name: Gunners
list.role: Three gunners, each on a gyro-stabilised turret on an outrigger, each with Fire and Missile. Every empty seat is an AI.

abilities.name: Sniper
abilities.text: The Serpent's sniper shot from the dorsal mast, the pip scope always open.

abilities.name: Fast gun
abilities.text: The Brittle Star's rounds from the port boom, 30 rounds/s while held.

abilities.name: Bomb
abilities.text: The Grizzly's trigger bomb from the starboard boom, one at a time.

cards.name: Breach
cards.description: Orca only, and the burn is the race. The helm's burn is five times your cruise, but a burning Orca turns wide and the tank refills slowly. Burn the straights and coast the turns - a burn into a hard turn misses the ring, and on the higher levels danger walls stand before some rings, rounded on the inside of the turn, and stop a hull dead. First team to put a pilot through the last ring takes it.

vessels.name: Starlings
vessels.description: A swarm, not a ship. The starlings roam the cell on their own after each objective in turn - the omnicrystal, elemental crystals, rival vessels, rival mass. You turn the view and pick one card from every hand; the cards you pick are what your swarm becomes.
vessels.note: the passive swarm card vessel: the swarm roams on its own, the pilot turns the view and picks cards: Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/STARLING.md

Charge.description: X: pick the Charge card from the hand. A hand is dealt when the Omnicrystal phase ends, or when the swarm collects an omnicrystal in another phase; a pick adds the card's level to what you hold of it (up to 15). R_VesselActions/STARLING.md.
notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Take the Charge card from a hand dealt to the swarm. Charge cards arm the swarm against rivals and wildlife - stings, lasers, chain lightning, a pulse - and a card you already hold levels up.
words.trigger: Tap while a hand is up
words.scales: Your Charge level does not change this; each card's own level sets its strength.

Mass.description: A: pick the Mass card from the hand. A hand is dealt when the Omnicrystal phase ends, or when the swarm collects an omnicrystal in another phase; a pick adds the card's level to what you hold of it (up to 15). R_VesselActions/STARLING.md.
notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Take the Mass card from a hand dealt to the swarm. Mass cards build and protect: the swarm lays your prisms, drips danger prisms, grows shells or breeds more members. A held card levels up.
words.trigger: Tap while a hand is up
words.scales: Your Mass level does not change this; each card's own level sets its strength.

Space.description: Y: pick the Space card from the hand. A hand is dealt when the Omnicrystal phase ends, or when the swarm collects an omnicrystal in another phase; a pick adds the card's level to what you hold of it (up to 15). R_VesselActions/STARLING.md.
notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Take the Space card from a hand dealt to the swarm. Space cards eat rival mass: members steal, burst or bite through shielded prisms, or the swarm splits to work two objectives. A held card levels up.
words.trigger: Tap while a hand is up
words.scales: Your Space level does not change this; each card's own level sets its strength.

Time.description: B: pick the Time card from the hand. A hand is dealt when the Omnicrystal phase ends, or when the swarm collects an omnicrystal in another phase; a pick adds the card's level to what you hold of it (up to 15). R_VesselActions/STARLING.md.
notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Take the Time card from a hand dealt to the swarm. Time cards make the swarm faster and nimbler, let members dodge hits, or shorten every phase so hands come sooner. A held card levels up.
words.trigger: Tap while a hand is up
words.scales: Your Time level does not change this; each card's own level sets its strength.

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle). No row of its own: the default thumb-lift profile.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

vessels.name: Jacks
vessels.description: Two jacks herd the cell's wildlife. Herding, run each jack with a thumb, lift it to leave a decoy, pull a trigger to dash both jacks to it, and call the herd. Netting, fly them, one fish under each thumb, with a net between them that opens as the sticks go apart. D-pad left or right switches between herding and netting.
vessels.note: the Jacks: two jacks that herd real fauna, one player: thumbs run them on the board, or fly them as the hull (two-thumb flight). Was "Marlin and Jacks"; the name Marlin is kept for a swordsman: Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/JACKS.md

Charge.description: Charge sets the share of the herd that is DANGER: none at -5, all of it at 15. A danger creature that touches a rival hull stings it (a Strike) and is spent.

upgrade.label: Attack
upgrade.description: The herd goes for rivals near it and bites any it touches.

notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Part of your herd turns dangerous. A danger creature that touches a rival hull stings it, scoring a hit, and is used up.
words.trigger: Passive - your herd touches a rival
words.scales: More Charge makes more of your herd dangerous, from none of it to all of it.

Mass.description: Herding, call the herd to the point between the jacks. Netting, toggle whether your creatures are drawn to the plane. Mass sets how fast the herd breeds: a birth takes the species' own feeds at -5 and a third of them at 15, and the herd never starves below its minimum size.

upgrade.label: Mass Clusters
upgrade.description: Every few seconds a creature of the herd lays a cluster of your mass.

notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Herding, the herd rushes to the point between your two jacks for a moment. Netting, it switches whether your creatures are pulled onto your plane.
words.scales: More Mass makes your herd breed faster, each birth costing less food.

Space.description: Herding, zoom out to the whole cell and back. Space widens the ring both jacks and the decoy push the herd out of; it is never smaller than a big thumb.

upgrade.label: Eat Shields
upgrade.description: The herd eats shielded prisms.

words.does: Herding, the view eases out to show the whole cell so you can find more creatures, and back in again. It does nothing while netting.
words.scales: More Space widens the ring your jacks and decoy push the herd away with.

Time.description: Herding, pull a trigger to lay the decoy at the jack on that side (on a phone, lift a thumb). Netting, pull a trigger to rush to the decoy at speed. There is always one decoy. Time makes the herd faster.

upgrade.label: Second Decoy
upgrade.description: A second decoy: each trigger has its own, laid by it while herding and rushed to by it while netting.

notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Herding, drop a decoy jack where one of your jacks stands; it keeps the herd away like a third jack. Netting, rush the whole ship to the decoy at speed.
words.scales: More Time makes your herd swim faster.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle). No row of its own: the default thumb-lift profile.
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: A jack or the hull that collects an omni crystal hatches a worm colony of your colour behind you, which eats prisms and creatures. A crystal caught in the net is carried, not collected.

cards.name: Decoy Run
cards.description: Jacks only, and barely any flying - herding. Swap to the jacks, run them past the ring and drop a decoy beyond it, centre them behind it, take off and fly to the decoy. Line two rings up and one flight takes both. On the hard levels each pair lies on its own tilted plane, so roll onto it first. The hardest level gives a second decoy for a hairpin. First team to put a pilot through the last ring takes it.

vessels.name: Honeyguide
vessels.description: Two seats, one hull, like the honeyguide bird and the honey badger it leads. The Honeyguide flies the hull and rides trails: touch a trail of a domain the battery holds, nose along it, and slip to its end. The Ratel plays the Dynamo, a hex puzzle: every pattern made charges the battery and fires its own card. D-pad left or right swaps seats; the AI takes the empty one.
vessels.note: the Honeyguide and Ratel: two seats on one hull (its own model on the Sparrow's airframe) with the Ratel's Dynamo seat: Controller/Vessel/Crew/HONEYGUIDE.md

Charge.description: Hold LT to see the dart, let go to fly it: 18 u ahead, striking every rival vessel and creature within 8 u of its lane, every 2 s. Each Charge card the Ratel makes (Hard Light Lasso, Blink Drive, All Terrain Portals, Rosen Bridge, FTL Chromatool, Monte Cannon) banks three uses on LT; the newest fires first.
notes: gate exists but the map names no upgrade

words.does: Hold to see the dart's line, let go to dart forward, striking every rival ship and creature along it. Each Charge card the Ratel makes on its puzzle banks three stronger uses.
words.scales: The map names no Charge scaling for the dart; Charge cards from the Ratel are what change it.

Mass.description: Every 45 s (sooner as Mass rises) a hive appears somewhere in the cell. Fly to it to open hive mode.
notes: gate exists but the map names no upgrade

words.does: Every so often a hive appears somewhere in the cell, marked by a turning hex frame. Fly into it and the Ratel's board becomes a hive puzzle that pays out prisms and charges.
words.scales: More Mass makes new hives appear sooner.

Space.description: Hold RT to see the aim line, let go for three quick shots, every 1 s. Each Space card the Ratel makes (Genesis Lance, Little Bang Grenade, Particle Harmonizer, Fugacity Discharger, Sepia Drone, Thruster Swarm, Hexapod Eyelet Jet) banks three uses on RT; the newest fires first. Hold both triggers to cancel.

upgrade.label: Piercing Pecks
upgrade.description: Pecks pierce through prisms instead of stopping at the first.

words.does: Hold to see the aim line, let go to fire three quick shots that chip away rival prisms ahead. Each Space card the Ratel makes banks three stronger uses.
words.scales: The map names no Space scaling for the pecks; Space cards from the Ratel are what change them.

Time.description: Touch a trail of a domain the battery holds with your nose along it and ride it to its end, fast: the charge is spent. The Ratel charges the battery by making patterns on the Dynamo.
notes: gate exists but the map names no upgrade

words.does: Touch a trail of a colour your battery holds with your nose along it and zip along it to its end. It spends that colour's charge, which the Ratel earns by making patterns.
words.scales: The map names no Time scaling for the slip itself.

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: The crystal turns into a hive comb behind you and the Ratel plays the hive puzzle. Your ship is shielded from elemental damage while hive mode lasts, and for 8 seconds besides.

list.name: Honeyguide
list.role: Flies the hull on the Sparrow's airframe. Its ride is the Slip; its two triggers are its own.

list.name: Ratel
list.role: Plays the Dynamo, a hex puzzle: a made pattern sends a prism to the battery as a slip charge and fires its card's effect; every four patterns the Ratel picks one of three abilities.

cards.name: Slip Line
cards.description: Honeyguide only, and the rails are the race. Touch a rail of a colour your battery holds with your nose along it and you zip down it eight times faster than you fly - one charge a ride. The Ratel makes the charges, so spend them well - stubs are not worth one, leaning rails need a turn out to meet, and on the hardest level one ride chains into the next. First team to put a pilot through the last ring takes it.

vessels.name: Meerkat
vessels.description: Digs its own way. The reticle on its nose is the tunnel it would form; bend it with the right stick, shorten it with LT, and RT ripples the wormhole open and dives you through it, out the far end with the speed you went in with. Everyone sees the bridge it leaves.
vessels.note: the wormhole vessel: one thumb flies, the right stick bends a tunnel, RT dives through it (24-27 are claimed on in-flight branches: Flea, Warden, Bulwark, Tempest): Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/MEERKAT.md

Charge.description: Y toggles it. While it is on, each new soliton leaves a sentinel at its way in, an afterimage of the hull that guards it: it zaps rivals in its guard (Charge sets the petals a zap knocks out, and the hit silences them) and shields your own prisms there. A soliton with a sentinel stands as long as its sentinel; with the pool of 3 used up, the oldest retires with its soliton. Garrett's design, approved by Yash 2026-10-28.

upgrade.label: Six Sentinels
upgrade.description: The pool is 6 sentinels.

words.does: While on, each new tunnel leaves a sentinel at its entrance that zaps rivals nearby, knocking out petals and silencing them, and shields your own prisms there. Its tunnel stands while it does.
words.scales: More Charge makes each sentinel zap knock out more of a rival's petals.

Mass.description: Passive: when your soliton forms it sets down six small prisms of your domain on a hexagon round its way out, at 1.5 x the exit's radius. Mass sets their size. Garrett's design, approved by Yash 2026-10-28.

upgrade.label: Danger Portal
upgrade.description: The exit portal's prisms are danger prisms.

words.does: Each tunnel you form sets six small prisms of your colour in a hexagon round its way out.
words.scales: More Mass makes the exit portal's prisms bigger.

Space.description: RT forms the wormhole the reticle shows, and it is a soliton: a standing tunnel anyone may ride. Its surface area is your Space level, so a long one is thin and a short one fat. It swallows prisms at its way in (shielded ones too, never super-shielded) and fires them out of its way out as moving prisms: one that hits a plain prism destroys both, scored to you; a shielded one bounces. Garrett's design, approved by Yash 2026-10-28.

upgrade.label: Steal
upgrade.description: Every prism your soliton swallows is stolen into your domain as its run starts, so it leaves the way out already yours.

notes: NO SCALING — this element changes no number

words.does: Form the tunnel your reticle shows and dive through it. It stays standing for Meerkats to ride, sucks in nearby prisms and fires them out the far end to smash other prisms for you.
words.scales: More Space gives every tunnel more surface, so a tunnel of any length comes out fatter.

Time.description: Passive: you ride every soliton faster, your own or anyone's (the throat's rush grows with Time). Garrett's design, approved by Yash 2026-10-28.

upgrade.label: Boost Out
upgrade.description: You leave every soliton with a boost (1.5 x the exit speed).

words.does: You rush through every tunnel faster, your own or another Meerkat's.
words.scales: More Time makes the rush through every tunnel stronger.

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Grows a network of branching wormhole tunnels from where you took the crystal that you can slide through; with full Mass it covers the whole cell.

cards.name: Burrow Run
cards.description: Meerkats only, and time is everything. The reticle on your nose is the tunnel you would dig - bend it toward the next ring with the right stick, shorten it with LT, and pull RT to ripple it open and dive through, out the far end with the speed you went in with. Eight rings a lap, two laps.

cards.name: Warpline
cards.description: Meerkats only, and time is everything. The reticle on your nose is the tunnel you would dig - bend it toward the next ring with the right stick, shorten it with LT, and pull RT to ripple it open and dive through, out the far end with the speed you went in with. Five long legs a lap, two laps.

vessels.name: Tiger Moth
vessels.description: Slow, wide and quiet, like the Butterfly - until a bat comes. Hold to shut your wings and drop the way your dust falls; let go and you fly on down the line you fell.
vessels.note: the Butterfly's airframe with the Drop (a tiger moth shuts its wings and drops): hold, fall along your own down while the camera rides above, land pitched into the line you fell: Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/TIGER_MOTH.md

Charge.description: DUST MODE (RT). The dust is ONE capsule hanging below the hull, live and drawn as falling motes only while the right trigger has switched the Butterfly into Dust mode. While an opposing pilot stays inside it, the dust SHREDS them: it steals ONE petal of ONE random element they hold, once a second at Charge 0 and ten times a second at Charge 10 (VesselElementalDebuffBySkimmerEffect, shredInterval 1 s -> 0.1 s, classed VesselContact so an arena ward cannot cancel it). Score and silence are priced per petal: each shred silences for one petal, and one Strike is scored per 3.2 petals shredded. An ALLY pilot it touches is CLEANSED: their silence lifts and their temporary debuffs end (the omni-crystal bloom cleanses its pilot and every ally its wavefront reaches, and a Drop made in Dust mode cleanses the pilot). An opposing lifeform's heart it reaches is killed (the wither); an ALLY lifeform is refreshed instead (Nourish - its starvation clock and breeding counter, never its size).

upgrade.label: Toll Gate
upgrade.description: Your wormhole strips the elements of opposing pilots who thread it, and wears your domain's hue.

words.does: In Dust mode your falling dust steals petals from any rival inside it, one at a time, scoring and silencing them. Allies it touches are cleansed; rival creatures it reaches wither.
words.trigger: Passive - keep a rival in your dust
words.scales: More Charge makes the dust steal petals faster, up to ten a second.

Mass.description: RIGHT TRIGGER toggles the Butterfly between two modes. MASS mode (the default) lays a WIDE wake: the trail prism widens to 5x at Mass 0 rising to 20x at Mass 15 (SpreadWingsActionSO.massModeWidth, eased over ~1.5s so a stroke reads as a stroke), and the dust is off. DUST mode narrows the wake back to a line of keys and switches the dust capsule on. Mass is the WIDTH of what you paint; the old per-prism trailVolume scaling is off on this hull so the two are not one number counted twice.

upgrade.label: Gilded Wake
upgrade.description: Mass mode lays SHIELDED prisms.

words.does: Switch between two modes. Mass mode paints a wide wake of prisms behind you with no dust; Dust mode narrows the wake to a line and turns on the dust below you.
words.scales: More Mass widens the wake you paint in Mass mode.

Space.description: The dust capsule's LENGTH is Space (the skimmer's Space-scaled Scale, elongated along the capsule axis only). What the dust does to MASS: an OWN-domain prism grows along a random axis, or turns DANGEROUS, or turns SHIELDED; an OPPOSING prism is destroyed, shrunk, or stolen. Each prism's outcome is a deterministic roll of that prism, so every peer agrees.

upgrade.label: Diamond Dust
upgrade.description: Dust on your own PLAIN mass occasionally raises a SUPER-SHIELD.

words.does: Your dust works on prisms too: your own grow, turn dangerous or get shielded, while rival prisms are destroyed, shrunk or stolen.
words.scales: More Space makes the dust that falls below you longer.

Time.description: HOLD. The wings shut and the hull falls belly-first along its own down - the way its dust rains - without turning, at 900 u/s, passing through everything (incorporeal: no prism, crystal, hull or wormhole touches it) and leaving no trail, while the camera swings up over it so the fall reads as flying forward. LET GO and it lands: the hull pitches 90 degrees nose-down into the line it fell on and flies straight on. No longest drop. The RECHARGE is paid by distance: a hop costs a little, a medium drop (900 u) the full 20 s, and anything past that is free. Only a full-recharge drop leaves a wormhole pair (neutral: everyone rides free until Charge 5). Time's dial is the recharge (half at Time 10).

upgrade.label: Afterburn
upgrade.description: For 3 s after the drop you stay incorporeal and fly a speed boost.

words.does: Shut your wings and fall straight down your belly line, passing through everything and leaving no trail. Let go to flip into the fall and fly on. A long drop leaves a wormhole pair.
words.scales: More Time shortens the drop's recharge, down to half at the top.

rows.pc: W A S D + P ; L '

notes: Phone: abilities on thumb lifts (left thumb = RT, right thumb = LT, both = idle).
Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: Sets off a huge bloom of dust: rivals in it lose petals of every element, rival prisms and creatures are blighted, your prisms are tended, and you and nearby allies are cleansed.

cards.name: Dustup
cards.description: Butterflies only, loose in the Boneyard, and not a gun between them. Flip to Dust mode and your scale dust hangs below you - fly OVER a rival and every element they have takes the bite. Charge makes it bite harder. One pass is one dusting; first team to the target wins.

cards.name: Sirocco
cards.description: Butterflies only, over Rampage's cactus forest. Flip to Dust mode and fly low - your scale dust shreds, shrinks or steals the other colours' plants and fortifies your own. Space lengthens the dust, so every Space crystal is a wider swath. First team to erode the target wins.

cards.name: Tapestry
cards.description: Butterflies only, and an empty sky to fill. Mass mode paints a wake many keys wide - Mass crystals widen your brush. Flip to Dust mode and fly over a rival's painting to shred it, shrink it or steal it for your own. When the clock runs out, the team with the most standing wins.

cards.name: Waystation
cards.description: Tiger Moths only. Weave each cluster of rings, then climb down the Drop Tower to the next: short hops through floor plates, each ring just past its plate. Tap too short and you land on the plate; hold too long and the pipe ahead meets you before the Drop is back. Plates are mostly plain at low intensity, more of them danger as it climbs. The last gap is one long drop, and it leaves a wormhole for whoever follows.

vessels.name: Swordfish
vessels.description: All sword. Your triggers swing a blade that cuts every prism it touches; hold both to light it, and a lit blade lays afterimages of itself. Run flat out and the ramp winds you up to the fastest top speed in the fleet.
vessels.note: all sword: the Rhino's blade, energize, afterimages and surge ring on the Rhino's airframe, split off the Rhino on 2026-11-07 (Garrett); the Rhino keeps the plough: Controller/Vessel/R_VesselActions/SWORDFISH.md

Charge.description: Hold both triggers to light the blade: it costs nothing and its cooldown is its only limit (the sword has had no energy meter since 2026-10-26). A lit blade lays the afterimages (Mass) and, with the Space level-5 upgrade, pops super-shielded prisms. Charge also scales how many petals a sword hit takes from a rival vessel - x1 at rest (the price Broadside puts on a Strike), x2.5 at level 10, floored at x1 (RhinoSwordStealBySkimmerEffect.stealScale, read at the thief's replicated level). Below Charge 5 those petals are knocked loose as crystals at the strike; the level-5 upgrade makes the sword pocket them.

upgrade.label: Sword Steal
upgrade.description: A sword hit on a rival vessel STEALS its petals - they land on the Swordfish instead of being knocked loose as crystals at the strike (the same verb and numbers as the Squirrel's joust). RhinoSwordStealBySkimmerEffect.stealUpgradeElement, gated on IsUpgradeActive(Charge) in VesselOvertakeBySkimmerEffectSO.TakeFrom (Garrett, 2026-10-26).

words.does: Hold both evenly for a second to light the sword. It stays lit while you hold, then for a few seconds after, followed by a short cooldown. It costs nothing. A sword hit on a rival knocks their petals loose as crystals.
words.scales: More Charge knocks more petals off a rival with each sword hit.

Mass.description: When the energized blade goes out, the sword keeps leaving copies of itself - prisms in the blade's own shape and pose - for 5 s (RhinoSwordAfterimage, RhinoSwordAfterimageConfig). The omni-crystal Surge (the crystal is absorbed into the hull; 8 s, a ring of eight trigger-driven swords round it) lays them for its whole length, from the pilot's blade. Mass scales their VOLUME: x1 at rest, x2.5 at level 10, floored at x0.25, read at the replicated level so every peer lays the same mass. They are not immune to the Swordfish's own blade: past the 1 s self-trail grace it cuts them like any prism.

upgrade.label: Danger Afterimages
upgrade.description: The afterimages are laid as DANGER prisms (RhinoSwordAfterimageConfigSO.dangerUpgradeElement, gated on IsUpgradeActive(Mass), snapshotted per afterimage).

words.does: When the lit sword goes out, it keeps leaving prism copies of itself in its own shape and pose for five seconds - walls you swing into place. Your own sword can still cut them.
words.scales: More Mass makes the afterimage prisms bigger.

Space.description: Space alone grows the sword: the blade runs 24 at rest to 40 at level 10 (Skimmer.Scale on the Swordfish's ForceFieldSkimmer, eased in by ShieldSkimmerScaleDriver), and nothing else resizes it - no energy, no surge burst (2026-10-26). The local pilot's camera pulls back with it, in proportion (ShieldSkimmerScaleConfig.cameraFollowsBladeLength), so the blade reads the same size on screen. Reach is what the blade cuts, what it strikes an Astro League ball with at the tip, and how far the afterimages and the surge's sword ring reach.

upgrade.label: Shield Breaker
upgrade.description: The sword can destroy SUPER-SHIELDED prisms: an energized blade pops them. Without the upgrade the blade binds in hardened mass, energized or not. ShieldSkimmerScaleConfigSO.superShieldUpgradeElement, gated on IsUpgradeActive(Space) (Garrett, 2026-10-26).

words.does: Your sword cuts any ordinary or shielded prism it touches, and you swing it by how hard you squeeze each side. Super-shielded mass makes the blade stick unless you have the upgrade.
words.scales: More Space makes the sword longer, and your camera pulls back to match.

Time.description: Time is the sword's RATE: it divides the energize hold (1 s at rest, 0.4 s at level 10), the energize cooldown (5 s -> 2 s) and each swipe's recovery (0.35 s -> 0.14 s), x1 at rest, x2.5 at level 10, floored at x0.5 (ShieldSkimmerScaleConfig.timeSwordRateMultiplier, RhinoShieldSwipeConfig.timeSwipeRateMultiplier, read live). The let-go tail stays 5 s. The Swordfish's own Time card since 2026-11-12, replacing the Ramp Spool it shared with the Rhino: its ramp still winds it to 840 u/s (SwordfishRampBoostAction), but no element scales the wind-up.

upgrade.label: Flurry
upgrade.description: The swipe recovery is gone for good: the sword swings as freely as an energized blade, lit or not (RhinoShieldSwipeConfigSO.flurryUpgradeElement, gated on IsUpgradeActive(Time) in ShieldSwipeActionExecutor.ApplySwipeRecovery). Replaces Momentum, which stays the Rhino's.

Tilt the phone to steer with no thumb down.

Only a controller has analog triggers: a key, a mouse button or a phone button is a full pull.

words.does: For 8 seconds your blade stays energized and a ring of swords surrounds the ship, swinging with your triggers, while the camera pulls back. A blast also breaks prisms round you.

cards.name: Astro League
cards.description: Hypersea soccer, played with a sword. Swordfish only - swing the blade through the payload and slam it into the enemy portal. Tip strikes hit hardest. First to five, golden goal if it's tied. Welcome to the league.

cards.name: Broadside
cards.description: Every hull that can fight, loose in the Boneyard, each with the weapon it actually has - a Sparrow's guns and rockets, an Urchin's spikes, a Swordfish's sword, a Squirrel's joust, a Dolphin's cone, a Scarab's plate, a Manta's bloom. A hit is worth what it cost you to land, not what you flew: a round is 1, a contact strike 8, a debuff 12, a rocket up to 30. First team to the target wins. Pick the hull you fight best.

cards.name: Brood Rush
cards.description: Hold the nucleus. Every brood the cell births in your color scores a point - first team to three wins.

cards.name: Cleave
cards.description: Four arenas, one blade. Angled panes, wide wavy roads, a cage of nested shells, and twisted ribbons that roll out from under you - every intensity is a different place to cut, not a bigger version of the last. Danger prisms ride the rims and the outside of the bends, so read the place before you commit.
